scenario: 面试官抛出一句「给 Airbnb 设计一个搜索排序系统」，没有任何约束，等你开口。
scenario_en: The interviewer drops 'design a search ranking system for Airbnb' with no constraints and waits for you to start.
q: 什么是「问题形式化(problem formulation)」，为什么它决定成败？
q_en: What is 'problem formulation,' and why does it decide success?
why: 问题形式化 = 把模糊的业务命题翻译成一个精确、可解的 ML 问题。形式化对了，后面每个决策都容易被追问时自证；形式化错了，架构再精巧也是在解错的问题。
why_en: Problem formulation is translating a vague business prompt into a precise, solvable ML problem; get it right and every downstream decision is easy to justify, get it wrong and even a sophisticated architecture solves the wrong problem.
diagram:
flowchart LR V["模糊业务命题
(intentionally vague)"] -->|结构化探索
problem formulation| P["精确可解的
ML 问题"] P --> D["每个下游决策
都可追溯自证"]
options: 问题形式化就是选定模型架构，越早定下用哪个模型越好
把模糊业务命题翻译成精确可解的 ML 问题
问题形式化是最后写评估指标的步骤，放在设计末尾即可
问题形式化是把需求写成代码接口，主要是工程活
options_en: Problem formulation means choosing the model architecture, and the earlier you fix the model the better.
Translating a vague business prompt into a precise, solvable ML problem.
Problem formulation is the final step of writing evaluation metrics, fine to leave for the end of the design.
Problem formulation is turning requirements into code interfaces — mostly an engineering task.
optionExplanations: 过早锁模型正是要避免的锚定：形式化是先定义问题，不是先选模型。
对；先把模糊命题收敛成一个精确 ML 问题，后面的架构、指标才有对的靶子。
指标是形式化的产物之一，但形式化本身发生在最前面，不是收尾步骤。
写接口是工程实现；形式化解决的是「到底要解哪个 ML 问题」这个更前置的判断。
optionExplanations_en: Locking the model early is exactly the anchoring to avoid: formulation defines the problem first, not the model.
Correct — converging the vague prompt into a precise ML problem first gives the architecture and metrics a correct target.
Metrics are an output of formulation, but formulation itself happens up front, not as a wrap-up step.
Writing interfaces is implementation; formulation answers the earlier question of which ML problem to solve at all.

scenario: 面试才刚开始几分钟，你在纠结要先展示哪个高级模型来抓住面试官。
scenario_en: Only a few minutes in, you're deciding which advanced model to showcase first to impress the interviewer.
q: 面试官对候选人的评估，权重最高的往往是哪个阶段？
q_en: Which phase carries the most weight in how interviewers assess candidates?
why: 面试官很大程度上看你开场那几分钟的结构化问题探索——这段早期 framing 往往比后面任何单个建模选择更影响评分。开局把问题框对，比秀一个高级模型更值钱。
why_en: Interviewers weigh the first few minutes of structured problem exploration heavily, and that early framing often matters more than any single modeling choice.
options: 开场几分钟的结构化问题探索(早期 framing)
中段选用的模型架构，越前沿新颖越能拉高整体评分
结尾的评估与监控方案，是打分的主要依据
全程的编码实现细节，写得越完整分越高
options_en: The first few minutes of structured problem exploration — the early framing.
The mid-session model architecture — the more cutting-edge, the higher the overall score.
The closing evaluation and monitoring plan is the main basis for scoring.
The coding implementation details throughout — the more complete, the higher the score.
optionExplanations: 对；开局的框定质量最能预示后面所有决策的可辩护性，权重自然最高。
秀前沿模型若没框对问题，反而暴露锚定；架构不是评分的重心。
评估重要，但它是形式化的下游产物，不是被最先、最重看的阶段。
编码完整度不是系统设计面的主要信号，判断力才是。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the quality of the opening framing predicts the defensibility of every later decision, so it carries the most weight.
Showcasing a cutting-edge model without framing the problem exposes anchoring; architecture isn't the scoring focus.
Evaluation matters but is a downstream product of formulation, not the first and most heavily weighted phase.
Coding completeness isn't the main signal in a system design round; judgment is.

scenario: 面试官给的命题「给 Airbnb 设计搜索排序」故意含糊，你不确定他是不是漏说了细节。
scenario_en: The prompt 'design search ranking for Airbnb' is deliberately vague, and you're unsure if the interviewer just left out details.
q: 「问题形式化 gap」指什么？含糊的命题是疏忽还是有意？
q_en: What is the 'problem-formulation gap,' and is a vague prompt an oversight or intentional?
why: 形式化 gap = 面试官那句「有意含糊」的命题，和你最终要解的那个具体 ML 问题之间的距离。含糊是故意的，用来考你导航歧义的能力——同一句命题会因优化目标、用户情境、延迟预算、冷启动比例分叉成完全不同的系统。
why_en: The formulation gap is the distance between the interviewer's intentionally ambiguous prompt and the specific ML problem you end up solving; the vagueness is deliberate, testing how you navigate ambiguity.
options: 指命题写得不够详细，属于面试官的疏忽，你应假设一个默认场景直接开做
指模型和数据之间的差距，靠加特征就能补上
有意含糊的命题与你要解的具体 ML 问题之间的距离
指线上和线下指标的差距，属于评估阶段的问题
options_en: It means the prompt lacks detail due to the interviewer's oversight, so assume a default scenario and just start building.
It means the gap between model and data, closable by adding features.
The distance between the intentionally vague prompt and the specific ML problem you end up solving.
It means the gap between online and offline metrics, an evaluation-stage concern.
optionExplanations: 把含糊当疏忽、直接假设默认场景，正是被考的反面——你会解到错的问题上。
这是把 gap 误当技术差距；形式化 gap 是命题到问题定义的距离，不是特征问题。
对；含糊是刻意设计的考点，你要主动把命题收敛成一个具体问题，而不是接受表面。
线上线下 gap 是另一个概念，不是命题到问题定义之间的这段形式化距离。
optionExplanations_en: Treating vagueness as oversight and assuming a default is exactly what's tested against — you'll solve the wrong problem.
This mistakes the gap for a technical gap; the formulation gap is prompt-to-problem-definition distance, not a feature issue.
Correct — the vagueness is a deliberate test, and you must actively converge the prompt into a specific problem rather than accept the surface.
The online-offline gap is a different concept, not this prompt-to-definition formulation distance.

scenario: 同一句「Airbnb 搜索排序」，业务目标定为「预订转化率」时，你要选一种建模形式。
scenario_en: For the same 'Airbnb search ranking,' with the business objective set to booking conversion, you must pick a modeling form.
q: 当优化目标是预订转化时，最直接的形式化是什么？
q_en: When the objective is booking conversion, what's the most direct formulation?
why: 优化目标决定形式化。目标是预订转化 → learning-to-rank，用「完成预订」当正样本标签排序。若目标换成长期房东满意度，就要变成多目标（预订率+评价分+房东留存），形式完全不同。
why_en: The optimization target drives formulation: booking conversion maps to learning-to-rank with completed bookings as the positive label, while long-term host satisfaction becomes a multi-objective problem.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务目标改成长期房东满意度，就该用多目标（预订率+评价分+房东留存），而不是单一预订转化的 LTR。
options: 多目标优化，同时平衡预订率、评价分和房东留存
learning-to-rank，正样本 = 完成预订
无监督聚类，把房源按相似度分组后按组整体推荐
回归预测每个房源的绝对价格，价高者排前
options_en: Multi-objective optimization balancing booking rate, review scores, and host retention at once.
Learning-to-rank, with completed bookings as the positive label.
Unsupervised clustering that groups listings by similarity and recommends by group.
Regression predicting each listing's absolute price, ranking higher-priced first.
optionExplanations: 多目标是「长期房东满意度」那个目标的形式化，对预订转化这个单目标是过度复杂化。
对；预订转化是明确的正/负信号，用完成预订当正标签的 LTR 直接对齐这个目标。
聚类没有利用预订这个监督信号，答不了「哪个更可能被订」。
预测绝对价格与「被预订概率」错位，价高不等于转化高。
optionExplanations_en: Multi-objective is the formulation for the host-satisfaction target; it over-complicates the single booking-conversion goal.
Correct — booking conversion is a clear positive/negative signal, so LTR with completed bookings as the positive label aligns directly.
Clustering ignores the booking supervision signal and can't answer which listing is more likely booked.
Predicting absolute price is misaligned with booking probability; higher price isn't higher conversion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 直接学习候选集的排序（而非独立打分）的一类方法，常用成对或列表损失，正样本是被点击/预订的项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learning to rank (LTR) learns to order a candidate set directly, often with pairwise or listwise loss, using clicked or booked items as positives.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时优化多个可能冲突的目标（如预订率、评价、房东留存），需要加权或帕累托权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-objective optimization jointly optimizes several possibly conflicting goals (booking rate, reviews, host retention) via weighting or Pareto trade-offs.

scenario: 同一个排序问题，延迟预算被确认为极紧的 50ms（对比另一场景是宽松的 500ms）。
scenario_en: For the same ranking problem, the latency budget is confirmed as a tight 50ms (versus a generous 500ms in another scenario).
q: 50ms 的延迟预算会把形式化推向什么，和 500ms 有何不同？
q_en: How does a 50ms budget steer the formulation, versus 500ms?
why: 延迟预算直接砍掉整类模型。50ms → 只能上轻量模型 + 预计算特征，来不及做重推理；500ms → 装得下更重的 re-ranking 阶段。同一个问题，预算不同就分叉成不同架构。
why_en: The latency budget prunes whole model classes: 50ms forces lightweight models with precomputed features, while 500ms leaves room for heavier re-ranking stages.
whenOtherWins: 如果预算是 500ms（如非首屏、可异步的场景），就能负担更重的 re-ranking，不必压到纯轻量模型。
options: 50ms 和 500ms 没有本质区别，模型选型只看精度，延迟只影响机器数量
50ms 允许更重的模型，因为预算紧反而要靠大模型一次算准
50ms 只能轻量模型+预计算；500ms 装得下重 re-ranking
50ms 意味着必须离线批处理，不能做在线推理
options_en: 50ms and 500ms are essentially the same; model choice depends only on accuracy, and latency just changes machine count.
50ms allows heavier models, because a tight budget means you need one big model to get it right in one shot.
At 50ms you only get lightweight models plus precomputed features; 500ms leaves room for a heavier re-ranking stage.
50ms means you must go offline batch and can't do online inference.
optionExplanations: 延迟恰恰是硬约束：它决定哪类模型根本来不及跑，不能只看精度。
说反了：预算越紧越用不起重模型，只能靠轻量模型+预计算把在线开销压下来。
对；50ms 逼你把重活挪到离线（预计算特征），线上只留轻量打分。
50ms 依然是在线推理，只是必须是轻量的；不等于退化成离线批处理。
optionExplanations_en: Latency is precisely the hard constraint: it decides which model classes can't run in time, not just accuracy.
Backwards: a tighter budget means you can't afford heavy models and must push cost offline with lightweight scoring.
Correct — 50ms forces the heavy work offline (precomputed features), leaving only lightweight scoring online.
50ms is still online inference, just lightweight; it doesn't degrade to offline batch.
tradeoff: 延迟预算 vs 模型容量：50ms 只买得起轻量模型+预计算，500ms 才装得下 re-ranking 阶段。
tradeoff_en: Latency budget vs model capacity: 50ms buys you only lightweight models plus precompute, while 500ms affords a re-ranking stage.

scenario: 澄清时你得知：Airbnb 每季度有约 40% 是全新房源（冷启动），而非稳定不变的存量。
scenario_en: You learn that about 40% of Airbnb listings each quarter are brand-new (cold-start), rather than stable inventory.
q: 40% 季度新房源这个事实，会怎样改变你的形式化？
q_en: How does 40% new listings per quarter change your formulation?
why: 40% 的季度新房源意味着大量物品没有交互历史，纯协同过滤会把它们冷落。它逼你做和稳定存量完全不同的特征工程：重内容特征（描述、图片、位置）而非依赖行为信号，否则新房源永远排不上去。
why_en: 40% new listings each quarter means many items have no interaction history, so you need content-based feature engineering rather than relying on behavioral signals, unlike a stable inventory.
options: 没有影响，新房源和老房源可以共用同一套行为特征来排序
大量物品无交互历史，逼你转向重内容特征的冷启动工程
意味着直接把新房源全部排到最后，等它们攒够点击再说
意味着改用回归预测房源价格，绕开冷启动
options_en: No impact — new and old listings can share the same behavioral features for ranking.
Many items have no interaction history, forcing content-heavy cold-start feature engineering.
It means simply ranking all new listings last until they accumulate enough clicks.
It means switching to regression on listing price to sidestep cold-start.
optionExplanations: 同一套行为特征对无历史的新房源是空的，40% 库存会被系统性埋没。
对；冷启动比例这么高，特征工程必须重内容侧（文本/图片/位置）来给新房源打分。
把新房源全排最后会伤害供给侧和用户体验，也不是解决冷启动的办法。
换回归改的是任务类型，回避不了「新房源没有信号」这个冷启动核心。
optionExplanations_en: The same behavioral features are empty for history-less new listings, systematically burying 40% of inventory.
Correct — with a cold-start ratio this high, feature engineering must lean on content (text/images/location) to score new listings.
Ranking all new listings last hurts supply and user experience and doesn't solve cold-start.
Switching to regression changes the task type but doesn't address the core cold-start issue of no signal for new listings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新用户或新物品缺乏历史交互，协同信号为空，需靠内容特征或探索来补。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold-start is when new users or items lack interaction history, so collaborative signals are empty and you rely on content features or exploration.

scenario: 澄清「搜索」的用户情境时，发现同一个搜索框既服务想订周末游的房客，也服务查看竞品定价的房东。
scenario_en: Clarifying the 'search' user context, you find the same box serves guests planning a weekend trip and hosts checking competitor pricing.
q: 为什么必须先分清「房客搜索」和「房东查竞品」这两种情境？
q_en: Why separate a guest's trip search from a host checking competitors first?
why: 两种用户意图完全不同：房客要可预订、匹配日期的房源，房东要的是竞品价格情报。意图不同 → 特征不同、指标不同，甚至是两个系统。不澄清就默认一种，等于赌一半概率解错问题。
why_en: Guest and host intents differ entirely — one wants bookable listings, the other wants competitor pricing — so features and metrics differ, and assuming one without asking risks solving the wrong problem.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官明确只做房客侧搜索，就可以把房东情境显式排除在范围外，聚焦单一意图。
options: 不用分，搜索框只有一个，两类用户可以共用同一排序逻辑
两种意图不同：可预订房源 vs 竞品价格情报，特征与指标都不同
因为房东用户更重要，应该优先只服务房东
因为要按用户所在地理位置分区，与用户意图本身无关
options_en: No need — there's one search box, so both user types can share the same ranking logic.
The two intents differ — bookable listings vs competitor pricing intel — so features and metrics differ.
Because host users matter more and should be served first and exclusively.
Because you should partition by the user's geography, which is unrelated to intent.
optionExplanations: 共用一套逻辑会两头不讨好：给房客的可预订排序满足不了房东的比价需求。
对；先分清意图，才知道该建哪套特征、用哪个指标，避免解错问题。
谁更重要是范围决策，但前提是先把两种意图分开、显式取舍。
地理分区是另一维度，回避不了「这是给房客还是房东用」这个意图问题。
optionExplanations_en: One shared logic satisfies neither: a guest's bookable ranking can't meet a host's price-comparison need.
Correct — separating intent first tells you which features and metric to use, avoiding solving the wrong problem.
Which matters more is a scoping decision, but only after explicitly separating the two intents.
Geographic partitioning is a different dimension and doesn't resolve the guest-vs-host intent question.
tradeoff: 房客意图 vs 房东意图：一边排可预订性、看预订转化，一边排竞品价格、看定价准确度，两套特征不共用。
tradeoff_en: Guest intent vs host intent: one ranks bookability and is judged on conversion, the other ranks competitor prices and is judged on pricing accuracy — the feature sets do not overlap.

rows: 可预订且日期匹配的房源

scenario: 命题刚说完，你的第一句话就在定调——面试官正据此判断你的级别。
scenario_en: Right after the prompt, your very first sentence sets the tone — the interviewer is already gauging your level.
q: 初级和资深候选人，对模糊命题的第一反应有何差别？
q_en: How do junior and senior candidates differ in their first response to a vague prompt?
why: 初级第一反应是报一个模型（「我会用 two-tower」）；资深第一反应是问业务目标和成功指标。先问目标的人才能把问题框对，报模型只是提前锚定。
why_en: A junior's first move is to name a model ('I'd use a two-tower'), while a senior first asks about the business objective and success metric.
tradeoff: 先报模型(显得果断但提前锚定) vs 先问目标/指标(慢半拍但框对问题)
options: 初级先问业务目标，资深先报一个模型架构
两者第一反应完全一样，只是资深讲得更流利
初级先报模型（two-tower），资深先问业务目标
初级先问延迟预算，资深先谈数据分布
options_en: Juniors first ask the business objective, seniors first name a model architecture.
Both react the same way; seniors just say it more fluently.
Juniors name a model first (two-tower); seniors ask about the business objective first.
Juniors first ask about the latency budget, seniors first discuss data distribution.
optionExplanations: 说反了：先问目标是资深行为，先报模型是初级的提前锚定。
第一反应的方向恰恰不同，这正是级别信号所在，不只是流利度。
对；先问目标与指标，后面所有决策才有可追溯的靶子，这是资深的开局。
延迟和数据是后续维度，第一反应的分水岭是「先报模型 vs 先问目标」。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: asking the objective first is the senior move; naming a model first is the junior's premature anchoring.
The direction of the first response is exactly what differs — that's the level signal, not just fluency.
Correct — asking objective and metric first gives every later decision a traceable target; that's the senior opening.
Latency and data are later dimensions; the dividing line at the first response is 'name a model vs ask the objective.'

scenario: 设计到一半，面试官挑战你：「为什么这里用两阶段而不是一把梭？」
scenario_en: Mid-design, the interviewer challenges: 'why two stages here instead of one pass?'
q: 被挑战时，初级和资深在「设计可辩护性」上差在哪？
q_en: When challenged, how do junior and senior differ in design defensibility?
why: 资深能把每个决策追溯回形式化阶段确立的某条需求（「我们定了 200ms 预算、100M 物品，所以排除一次过重打分」）；初级在被挑战时讲不出所以然，因为决策没锚在需求上。
why_en: A senior traces every decision back to a requirement set during formulation, while a junior can't justify choices when challenged because they weren't anchored to requirements.
tradeoff: 决策锚在需求上(可被追溯自证) vs 决策靠直觉/惯例(被挑战即失守)
options: 初级能追溯到需求，资深只会说这是常见模式
资深把决策追溯回形式化确立的需求，初级讲不出理由
两者都能自证，只是资深用词更专业
初级更敢坚持己见，所以更能辩护
options_en: Juniors trace to requirements, seniors just say it's a common pattern.
Seniors trace each decision back to a requirement fixed during formulation; juniors can't say why.
Both can justify; seniors just use more professional wording.
Juniors are more willing to hold their ground, so they defend better.
optionExplanations: 说反了：靠「常见模式」搪塞是初级，追溯需求才是资深。
对；决策一开始就锚在需求上，被追问时才能一句话把它拎回约束、自证成立。
关键不是用词，而是有没有可追溯的需求链；这决定了能不能真正辩护。
嘴硬不是辩护；没有需求支撑的坚持一被挑战就塌。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: falling back on 'common pattern' is junior; tracing to requirements is senior.
Correct — anchoring decisions to requirements from the start lets you pull them back to a constraint in one line when pressed.
The point isn't wording but whether there's a traceable requirement chain; that's what enables real defense.
Stubbornness isn't defense; conviction without a requirement basis collapses under challenge.

scenario: 被问「你打算用什么离线指标衡量这个排序系统」时，你的答法暴露级别。
scenario_en: Asked 'what offline metric will you use for this ranker,' your answer reveals your level.
q: 在指标定义上，初级和资深候选人的差别是什么？
q_en: How do junior and senior candidates differ on metric definition?
why: 初级默认套 accuracy 或 AUC；资深把离线指标绑定到一个业务 KPI，并会讨论校准(calibration)。离线指标脱离业务 KPI，就算离线涨了线上也未必赚钱。
why_en: A junior defaults to accuracy or AUC, while a senior ties the offline metric to a business KPI and discusses calibration.
tradeoff: 默认 accuracy/AUC(离线好看但可能脱离业务) vs 绑定业务 KPI + 校准(离线涨对应线上赚)
options: 初级绑定业务 KPI，资深只看 accuracy
两者都用 AUC，只是资深会额外多画一条 PR 曲线看尾部
初级默认 accuracy/AUC，资深绑定业务 KPI
资深只关心线上 A/B 实验，从不看任何离线指标
options_en: Juniors tie to a business KPI, seniors only watch accuracy.
Both use AUC; seniors just add a PR curve to inspect the tail.
Juniors default to accuracy/AUC; seniors tie it to a business KPI.
Seniors only care about online A/B tests and never look at any offline metric.
optionExplanations: 说反了：默认 accuracy 是初级，绑定 KPI 是资深。
多画曲线不是重点，重点是离线指标有没有对齐业务 KPI。
对；离线指标要能代理业务 KPI，还要校准，才能保证离线涨=线上有价值。
资深两者都看：离线快速迭代、线上最终验证，不是二选一。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: defaulting to accuracy is junior; tying to a KPI is senior.
Adding a curve isn't the point; the point is whether the offline metric aligns with the business KPI.
Correct — the offline metric must proxy the business KPI and be calibrated, so an offline gain means online value.
Seniors watch both: offline for fast iteration, online for final validation — not either/or.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量分类器把正样本排在负样本前的能力的离线指标，是技术指标不等于业务价值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) is an offline metric of a classifier's ability to rank positives above negatives — technical, not business value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型预测的概率与真实发生频率一致的程度（说 0.7 就真有约 70% 发生）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration is how well predicted probabilities match real frequencies — a 0.7 prediction should occur about 70% of the time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量业务成败的核心指标（如转化率、留存），离线指标应对齐它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A KPI (Key Performance Indicator) is a core business success metric like conversion or retention, which the offline metric should align to.

scenario: 一听到「欺诈检测」，你脑子立刻蹦出一套背好的架构：XGBoost + 规则兜底 + 流式处理，感觉很顺。
scenario_en: Hearing 'fraud detection,' your brain instantly surfaces a memorized stack: XGBoost + rule fallback + streaming, and it feels smooth.
q: 这种「秒出架构」的锚定为什么危险？
q_en: Why is this instant-architecture anchoring dangerous?
why: 锚定偏差让你把之后所有推理都拿来「合理化最初那个选择」，于是当面试官探一个你未验证假设覆盖不到的边缘情况时，你无法转向。更坏的是它感觉像自信和推进，不像犯错，所以最难自察。
why_en: Anchoring bias makes you filter all later reasoning to justify the initial choice, so you can't pivot when the interviewer probes an edge case your unvalidated assumptions miss — and it feels like confidence, not a mistake.
diagram:
flowchart TD P["听到'欺诈检测'"] --> A["秒出背好的架构
XGBoost+规则+流式"] A --> F["之后所有推理
都在合理化它"] F --> E["面试官探边缘情况"] E --> X["无法转向 → 失守"]
options: 危险在于 XGBoost 太老，应该锚定一个更新的模型
不危险，秒出架构说明你准备充分、反应快
锚定让你只为合理化初始选择，被追问边缘情况时无法转向
危险仅在于流式处理太贵，换成批处理就没问题
options_en: The danger is that XGBoost is too old; anchor on a newer model instead.
Not dangerous — an instant architecture shows you're well-prepared and quick.
Anchoring makes you rationalize the initial choice, so you can't pivot when an edge case is probed.
The danger is only that streaming is expensive; switch to batch and it's fine.
optionExplanations: 问题不在模型新旧，而在你还没框问题就锁死了方案。
秒出架构恰恰是锚定信号：快不等于框对了问题。
对；锚定的坏处是锁死推理方向、无法转向，且伪装成自信让你察觉不到。
换批处理没触及根因：根因是过早锁定、丧失转向能力，不是某个组件贵。
optionExplanations_en: The issue isn't the model's age but locking a solution before framing the problem.
An instant architecture is exactly the anchoring signal: fast doesn't mean you framed the problem right.
Correct — anchoring locks your reasoning direction and kills the ability to pivot, disguised as confidence so you don't notice.
Switching to batch misses the root cause: premature lock-in and lost pivot ability, not one expensive component.

termDefinitions.meaning: 过早认定一个方案后，把后续所有信息都往合理化它的方向解读，丧失转向能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Anchoring bias is fixating on an early choice and interpreting all later information to justify it, losing the ability to pivot.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种梯度提升树模型，表格数据上强、可解释、上线快，常被当欺诈检测的默认选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XGBoost is a gradient-boosted tree model, strong and interpretable on tabular data, often a default choice for fraud detection.

scenario: 你意识到自己一听命题就想秒出架构，想在开局就防住锚定这个最贵的失败模式。
scenario_en: You notice the urge to blurt an architecture on hearing the prompt, and want to guard against anchoring — the costliest failure mode — from the start.
q: 开局对抗锚定，最有效的做法是什么？
q_en: What's the most effective way to counter anchoring at the opening?
why: 锚定最贵是因为它感觉像自信和推进，而不像错误，所以最难当场察觉。对治办法是刻意延后锁定方案：先花 5–8 分钟做需求工程、把问题框清楚，让方案从需求里长出来，而不是反过来用需求合理化预设方案。
why_en: Anchoring is costly because it feels like confidence, not a mistake, so the counter is to deliberately delay committing — spend 5-8 minutes on requirements first and let the solution emerge from them.
whenOtherWins: 如果命题本身极窄、约束已给全（罕见），确实可以更快进入方案，但这种情况在开放式面试里几乎不出现。
options: 一想到架构就赶紧说出来，抢在忘记前把它讲完
刻意延后锁定：先做 5–8 分钟需求工程再谈方案
把脑中第一个架构默认当对的，再倒推需求去支持它
同时抛出三四个候选架构，让面试官帮你选一个
options_en: Say the architecture the instant it comes to mind, before you forget it.
Deliberately delay committing: do 5-8 minutes of requirements engineering before naming a solution.
Treat the first architecture in your head as correct and back-fill requirements to support it.
Throw out three or four candidate architectures and let the interviewer pick one.
optionExplanations: 抢着说出来正是锚定：一旦出口，你后面会不自觉地只为它辩护。
对；先做需求工程、延后锁定，方案由约束推导而来，天然可辩护也能随探问转向。
倒推需求支持预设方案就是锚定的定义，最危险。
一次抛多个方案不是框问题，是把选择权外包，仍没做形式化。
optionExplanations_en: Blurting it out is anchoring itself: once said, you'll unconsciously only defend it.
Correct — doing requirements first and delaying commitment makes the solution derive from constraints, naturally defensible and able to pivot.
Back-filling requirements to fit a preset solution is the definition of anchoring — the most dangerous.
Throwing out several at once isn't framing the problem; it outsources the choice and still skips formulation.

scenario: 你想把开局的探索控制在一个合理时长，既框清问题又不至于问到面试官打断。
scenario_en: You want to time-box the opening exploration so you frame the problem without the interviewer having to cut you off.
q: 资深候选人通常把开局多长时间当作「需求工程阶段」？
q_en: How long do senior candidates treat as the 'requirements engineering' phase up front?
why: 资深把开局约 5–8 分钟当成需求工程阶段，先探索再承诺架构。这是经验时长而非公式：太短会漏约束、太长会被面试官叫停；它决定了你留给后续架构/建模的时间预算。
why_en: Seniors treat roughly the first 5-8 minutes as a requirements-engineering phase, exploring before committing to architecture — a rule-of-thumb window, not a formula.
options: 整场的一半时间，约 20 分钟，越久越稳
约 5–8 分钟，先做需求工程探索再承诺架构
开局 1 分钟就够，问一两句立刻进方案
不设时长，想到哪问到哪直到面试官满意
options_en: Half the session, about 20 minutes — the longer the safer.
About 5-8 minutes of requirements-engineering exploration before committing to architecture.
One minute is enough — ask a question or two and jump straight into the solution.
No time box — keep asking whatever comes to mind until the interviewer is satisfied.
optionExplanations: 20 分钟太久，会挤掉架构和深挖的时间，面试官多半会叫停。
对；5–8 分钟够把五个维度探一遍，又给后面 35+ 分钟留出架构与建模空间。
1 分钟框不清问题，容易漏掉决定性约束，滑向锚定。
无时长控制会被面试官打断，反而暴露你不会管理节奏。
optionExplanations_en: 20 minutes is too long, crowds out architecture and deep dives, and the interviewer will likely stop you.
Correct — 5-8 minutes covers the five dimensions while leaving 35+ minutes for architecture and modeling.
One minute can't frame the problem, misses decisive constraints, and slides into anchoring.
No time box gets you interrupted and reveals poor pacing control.

scenario: 同是欺诈类问题：一个场景 chargeback 标签 24 小时内到，另一个欺诈要 90 天才被确认。
scenario_en: Two fraud-like problems: in one, chargeback labels arrive within 24 hours; in another, fraud is confirmed only after 90 days.
q: 标签延迟从 24 小时变成 90 天，为什么会变成「两个不同的问题」？
q_en: Why does a label delay of 24 hours versus 90 days make it 'two different problems'?
why: 标签延迟决定训练能拿到什么监督信号。24 小时到的标签近乎实时可训；90 天才确认意味着你训练时手里全是「还没盖棺」的样本，必须按延迟反馈来设计（等待期、代理标签、样本重加权），是完全不同的形式化。
why_en: Label delay decides what supervision you have at training time: 24-hour labels are near-real-time, while 90-day confirmation forces delayed-feedback design (waiting windows, proxy labels, reweighting).
whenOtherWins: 如果标签很快且可靠（24 小时到位），就不必上延迟反馈那套复杂设计，直接用近实时监督即可。
options: 标签延迟只影响上线速度，不改变问题的形式化
90 天延迟意味着训练样本大多未盖棺，必须按延迟反馈设计
延迟越长数据越干净，所以 90 天的问题反而更简单
只要多雇标注员，90 天延迟就能压到 24 小时
options_en: Label delay only affects deployment speed, not the problem's formulation.
A 90-day delay means most training samples aren't final yet, forcing delayed-feedback design.
Longer delay means cleaner data, so the 90-day problem is actually simpler.
Just hire more annotators and the 90-day delay compresses to 24 hours.
optionExplanations: 延迟不只是上线快慢：它改变你训练时能拿到多少确定标签，直接重塑形式化。
对；90 天意味着大量样本标签未定，得设计等待期/代理标签/重加权，是另一套问题。
延迟长不等于更干净，反而带来大量未定标签，问题更难不是更简单。
chargeback 的 90 天是业务确认周期，加人也压不动，这不是标注人力问题。
optionExplanations_en: Delay isn't just deployment speed: it changes how many confirmed labels you have at training time, reshaping the formulation.
Correct — 90 days means many samples are unresolved, needing waiting windows/proxy labels/reweighting — a different problem.
Longer delay isn't cleaner; it brings many unresolved labels, making the problem harder, not simpler.
The 90-day chargeback is a business confirmation cycle; more headcount can't compress it — it's not a labeling-labor issue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持卡人向银行申诉撤销一笔交易，常作为欺诈的延迟真值标签。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A chargeback is a cardholder disputing a transaction with the bank, often used as a delayed ground-truth fraud label.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标签在预测很久之后才到达，训练必须处理大量暂时无标签或标签会翻转的样本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delayed feedback is when labels arrive long after prediction, so training must handle many temporarily unlabeled or later-flipping samples.

tradeoff: 标签新鲜度 vs 监督信号完整性：24 小时标签可近实时训练，90 天则要用代理标签和等待期换准确标签。
tradeoff_en: Label freshness vs supervision completeness: 24-hour labels let you train near-real-time, while 90-day labels force proxy labels and waiting periods to buy accurate supervision.

scenario: 需求探索阶段，你在纠结要不要花一个问题去确认「现在线上有没有一套规则系统在跑」。
scenario_en: During exploration you're debating whether to spend a question confirming 'is there already a rule-based system in production.'
q: 为什么该问「现有 baseline 是什么」？它揭示了什么？
q_en: Why ask 'what's the current baseline,' and what does it reveal?
why: 问现有 baseline（比如已有规则系统）揭示了「增量改进」长什么样：你的模型不是从零证明价值，而是要打败一条现有基线。它决定成功标准、A/B 对照组，甚至要不要先复刻规则再叠加 ML。
why_en: Asking about the current baseline (e.g. an existing rule system) reveals what incremental improvement looks like — your model must beat a baseline, which sets the success bar and the A/B control.
whenOtherWins: 如果确认是全新产品、线上无任何 baseline，那成功标准就变成绝对值（如首次达到某召回/精度），而非相对提升。
options: 不必问，反正 ML 模型一定比规则强，直接替换即可
它揭示增量改进的样子：模型必须打败现有基线
问它只是礼貌，对设计没有实际影响
它主要用来估算数据量，和成功标准无关
options_en: No need to ask — an ML model always beats rules, so just replace it.
It reveals what incremental improvement means: your model must beat the existing baseline.
Asking is just politeness with no real design impact.
It's mainly for estimating data volume, unrelated to the success bar.
optionExplanations: 「一定更强」是危险假设：很多规则系统很强，ML 未必稳赢，忽视 baseline 会定错成功标准。
对；有 baseline，成功就变成相对提升，直接决定对照组、指标门槛和上线策略。
它有实打实的设计影响：没有它你都不知道要打败什么、涨多少才算成功。
它首先决定成功标准（要超过基线多少），估数据量是次要的。
optionExplanations_en: 'Always stronger' is a dangerous assumption: many rule systems are strong, ML may not win, and ignoring the baseline sets the wrong success bar.
Correct — with a baseline, success becomes a relative lift, directly setting the control group, metric threshold, and rollout strategy.
It has real design impact: without it you don't even know what to beat or how much lift counts as success.
It primarily sets the success bar (how much you must beat the baseline); estimating data volume is secondary.
tradeoff: 从零证明价值 vs 打败现有基线：有 baseline 时成功标准变成增量提升，但也把 A/B 对照组和上线门槛钉死了。
tradeoff_en: Proving value from scratch vs beating an existing baseline: with a baseline the success bar becomes incremental lift, but it also fixes your A/B control and launch threshold.

scenario: 面试官问「你为什么用两阶段 retrieval-ranking，而不是一次过打分？」你要展示一条从约束到方案的追溯链。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks 'why two-stage retrieval-ranking instead of one-pass scoring?' and you must show a constraint-to-decision trace.
q: 把「探索模式」候选人追溯这个决策的推理链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the exploration-mode candidate's reasoning chain for this decision:
steps: 所以选两阶段：先轻量 retrieval 缩小候选，再重模型 ranking
形式化时已确立约束：200ms 预算、100M 物品
被挑战时能一句话追溯回约束，决策站得住
推出：一次过用重模型给 1 亿物品打分，装不进 200ms
why: 探索模式的力量在于每个决策都能倒放回一条既定约束：200ms + 100M 物品 → 一次过重打分不可行 → 两阶段 → 被挑战时可自证。解决方案模式的候选人只能说「这是常见套路」，一挑就塌。
why_en: Exploration mode lets every decision replay back to a stated constraint — 200ms plus 100M items rules out one-pass heavy scoring, forcing two stages, so it holds up when challenged.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["约束: 200ms + 100M 物品"] --> R["一次过重打分
装不进 200ms"] R --> T["两阶段: retrieval → ranking"] T --> D["被挑战可追溯自证"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用轻量模型从海量物品召回少量候选(retrieval)，再用重模型对候选精排(ranking)，兼顾规模与精度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-stage retrieval-ranking first recalls a small candidate set from a huge corpus with a light model, then precisely ranks it with a heavy model, balancing scale and accuracy.

scenario: 面对「为什么两阶段？」这个追问，探索模式和解决方案模式的候选人给出的答法截然不同。
scenario_en: To the follow-up 'why two stages,' exploration-mode and solution-mode candidates answer very differently.
q: 「探索模式」和「解决方案模式」候选人的答法差在哪？
q_en: How do exploration-mode and solution-mode candidates' answers differ?
why: 探索模式答：「我们定了 200ms 预算、100M 物品，所以排除一次过重打分」——把决策接回约束。解决方案模式只能答「这是常见模式」——没有可追溯的理由，一被追问就露怯。
why_en: Exploration mode answers by tracing the decision to a constraint ('we set a 200ms budget with 100M items, ruling out one-pass heavy scoring'), while solution mode can only say 'it's a common pattern.'
tradeoff: 追溯到约束(可自证、抗追问) vs 诉诸常见模式(无理由、一挑即塌)
options: 探索模式说「这是常见模式」，解决方案模式追溯到约束
两者给出的答案其实一样，只是语气和自信程度不同
探索模式能把决策追溯回已定约束，方案模式只会说「常见模式」
解决方案模式答得更详细，所以更有说服力
options_en: Exploration mode says 'it's a common pattern,' solution mode traces to constraints.
Both give the same answer, differing only in tone and confidence.
Exploration mode traces the decision back to the agreed constraints; solution mode only says 'it's a common pattern.'
Solution mode answers in more detail, so it's more convincing.
optionExplanations: 说反了：追溯约束是探索模式，「常见模式」是解决方案模式。
答案的实质不同：一个有约束支撑、一个没有，这才是关键。
对；能把「两阶段」拎回 200ms+100M 的人，才在展示真正的形式化功力。
「常见模式」再详细也没有理由链，追问下反而更快露馅。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: tracing to constraints is exploration mode; 'common pattern' is solution mode.
The substance differs: one is constraint-backed and one isn't — that's the crux.
Correct — pulling 'two stages' back to 200ms+100M is what shows real formulation skill.
'Common pattern' has no reasoning chain no matter how detailed, and collapses faster under follow-up.

scenario: 你想要一份可复用的探索清单，保证开局 5–8 分钟不漏掉决定性维度。
scenario_en: You want a reusable exploration checklist so the opening 5-8 minutes never misses a decisive dimension.
q: 结构化探索清单包含哪些维度？(多选)
q_en: Which dimensions belong to the structured exploration checklist? (multiple)
why: 五维清单：业务目标、ML 任务定义、数据全景、系统约束、范围决策。每一维都会改写下游设计——漏掉任一维，就留下一个日后要付昂贵中途返工代价的盲点。「选哪家云厂商」不是形式化维度。
why_en: The five dimensions are business objective, ML task definition, data landscape, system constraints, and scope decision; each reshapes the downstream design.
options: 业务目标：主 KPI、次级指标、干系人优先级
ML 任务定义：分类/排序/生成，单任务还是多目标，在线还是离线推理
系统约束：延迟 SLA、吞吐 QPS、成本预算、容错
选哪家云厂商：AWS 还是 GCP 更便宜
options_en: Business objective: primary KPI, secondary metrics, stakeholder priorities.
ML task definition: classification/ranking/generation, single-task vs multi-objective, online vs offline inference.
System constraints: latency SLA, throughput QPS, cost budget, fault tolerance.
Which cloud vendor: whether AWS or GCP is cheaper.
optionExplanations: 对；业务目标塑造损失函数和评估框架，是清单第一维，必须最先探。
对；任务类型决定损失、指标和 serving 架构，是形式化的核心一维。
对；延迟/吞吐/成本/容错这些系统约束能直接砍掉整类模型。
错；选云厂商是实现层采购决策，不改变问题形式化，不属于探索维度。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the business objective shapes the loss and eval framework; it's the first dimension and must be explored first.
Correct — the task type sets loss, metric, and serving architecture, a core formulation dimension.
Correct — latency/throughput/cost/fault-tolerance constraints can cut whole model classes.
Incorrect — picking a cloud vendor is an implementation-layer procurement choice that doesn't change the formulation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 明确哪些功能纳入、哪些显式排除，以及先做 MVP 还是完整系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A scope decision fixes what's in, what's explicitly excluded, and whether to build an MVP or the full system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标签可得性、特征来源、数据新鲜度与体量的整体盘点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The data landscape is the overall picture of label availability, feature sources, data freshness, and volume.

分类/排序/生成"] B --> C["数据全景
标签来源与延迟"] C --> D["系统约束

scenario: 你在某处选了最终一致性而非强一致性，面试官问「凭什么？」，系统需要 50K TPS 且亚 100ms 延迟。
scenario_en: You chose eventual over strong consistency somewhere, and the interviewer asks 'on what basis?' — the system needs 50K TPS at sub-100ms.
q: 为什么「50K TPS @ 亚 100ms」这条约束能让「选最终一致性」变得可辩护？
q_en: Why does '50K TPS at sub-100ms' make choosing eventual consistency defensible?
why: 强一致性要跨节点协调（CAP 里的一致性），协调开销会顶破亚 100ms 的延迟 SLA。把「选最终一致性」追溯到 50K TPS + 亚 100ms 这条已定约束，它就从「拍脑袋」变成「被约束逼出来的必然」，可自证。
why_en: Strong consistency needs cross-node coordination whose overhead (CAP) breaks the sub-100ms SLA, so tracing 'eventual consistency' back to the 50K TPS at sub-100ms constraint makes it a forced, defensible choice.
options: 因为最终一致性永远比强一致性好，和约束无关
强一致的跨节点协调(CAP)会顶破亚 100ms SLA
因为 TPS 越高就必须用强一致性，这里数字不够所以退而求其次
因为一致性只影响存储成本，不影响延迟
options_en: Because eventual consistency is always better than strong, independent of constraints.
Because strong consistency's cross-node coordination breaks the sub-100ms SLA.
Because higher TPS forces strong consistency, and here the numbers are too low so you settle for less.
Because consistency only affects storage cost, not latency.
optionExplanations: 没有「永远更好」：最终一致性是被延迟约束逼出来的，脱离约束就不成立。
对；把决策接回具体约束，理由从「个人偏好」升级为「约束下的必然」，这就是可辩护。
说反了：高吞吐+低延迟恰恰逼你放弃强一致性的协调开销。
一致性直接影响延迟：强一致要等跨节点确认，正是它顶破 SLA 的原因。
optionExplanations_en: There's no 'always better': eventual consistency is forced by the latency constraint and doesn't hold without it.
Correct — tracing the decision to a concrete constraint upgrades the reason from preference to a constraint-forced necessity, which is defensibility.
Backwards: high throughput plus low latency is exactly what forces you to drop strong consistency's coordination overhead.
Consistency directly affects latency: strong consistency waits for cross-node acknowledgment, which is what breaks the SLA.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区发生时，一致性与可用性不可兼得；追求强一致要付跨节点协调延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says under a network partition you can't have both consistency and availability; strong consistency costs cross-node coordination latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒事务数，衡量系统吞吐；这里 50K TPS 是给定的规模约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TPS (Transactions Per Second) measures throughput; here 50K TPS is a given scale constraint.

scenario: 探索时你确认了一堆需求，但担心讲到后面会忘、或面试官看不出你在用它们。
scenario_en: You've confirmed a pile of requirements during exploration but worry you'll forget them or the interviewer won't see you using them.
q: 探索阶段确认的需求，最该怎么处理？
q_en: What's the best thing to do with requirements confirmed during exploration?
why: 把需求当场写下来（编号需求清单/共享文档），后面显式回指它们。这条可见的「决策审计轨迹」既帮你自己不跑偏，也让面试官看到你每个决策都挂在需求上——是面试官会主动奖励的行为。
why_en: Write requirements down as you confirm them and refer back to them explicitly; that visible decision audit trail is a behavior interviewers reward.
options: 记在脑子里就好，写下来会浪费宝贵的白板空间
当场写成编号需求清单，后面显式回指
只在最后总结时一次性列出来，中途不用提
全部交给面试官记录，自己专注讲方案
options_en: Just keep them in your head; writing wastes precious whiteboard space.
Write them down as a numbered requirements list and refer back to them explicitly.
List them only in the final summary and don't mention them mid-way.
Let the interviewer record everything while you focus on the solution.
optionExplanations: 只记脑子里，讲到后面容易漏、也让面试官看不见你在用需求。
对；写下来+回指，把「我在按需求做决策」变成可见证据，这正是被奖励的审计轨迹。
只在结尾列不产生中途的追溯效果，决策与需求的挂钩看不见。
让面试官记录等于放弃主导权，你应自己维护这条轨迹。
optionExplanations_en: Head-only means you'll drop some later and the interviewer won't see you using them.
Correct — writing plus referring back turns 'I'm deciding by requirements' into visible evidence, the rewarded audit trail.
Listing only at the end gives no mid-session traceability; the decision-to-requirement link stays invisible.
Letting the interviewer record cedes leadership; you should maintain the trail yourself.
diagram:
flowchart LR Q["探索问出的约束"] --> L["白板上编号需求清单
R1 延迟 200ms / R2 100M 物品"] L --> D["每个设计决策
显式回指 R1/R2"] D --> T["可见的决策审计轨迹"]

scenario: 你在犹豫要不要花时间探索——毕竟直接进方案感觉更快、更能展示技术。
scenario_en: You hesitate to spend time exploring — jumping to the solution feels faster and more technical.
q: 结构化探索为什么能实打实降低「设计风险」？
q_en: Why does structured exploration actually reduce 'design risk'?
why: 探索先把关键约束确认清楚，就避免了那种最贵的中途返工：设计到一半发现某个假设的约束是错的，被迫推倒重来。前期多花 5–8 分钟，省掉的是中段大改的时间和信任崩塌。
why_en: Exploration confirms key constraints up front, avoiding the expensive mid-interview pivot where an assumed constraint turns out wrong and forces a rebuild.
options: 因为探索能让你显得更资深，和设计风险无关
先确认关键约束，避免设计到一半发现假设错误、被迫返工
因为探索时间越长，最终模型精度越高
因为探索能替代后面的评估阶段，省掉一步
options_en: Because exploration makes you look more senior, unrelated to design risk.
Because it locks the key constraints first, avoiding an expensive rewrite when an assumption turns out wrong mid-design.
Because the longer you explore, the higher the final model accuracy.
Because exploration replaces the later evaluation phase, saving a step.
optionExplanations: 显得资深是副产品；降低设计风险的实质是提前排掉错误假设。
对；把约束验在前面，就不会在中段因假设崩塌被迫大改，这才是省风险的机制。
探索不直接提精度，它降低的是「解错问题/中途返工」的风险。
探索和评估是不同阶段，前者不替代后者。
optionExplanations_en: Looking senior is a byproduct; the real risk reduction is ruling out wrong assumptions early.
Correct — validating constraints up front prevents a mid-session rebuild when assumptions collapse, which is the risk-saving mechanism.
Exploration doesn't directly raise accuracy; it lowers the risk of solving the wrong problem or a mid-course pivot.
Exploration and evaluation are different phases; the former doesn't replace the latter.

scenario: 你把开局的形式化做得很扎实，后面偶尔出了个小口误或小疏漏。
scenario_en: You nailed the opening formulation, then later made a small slip or minor omission.
q: 扎实的开局探索，对面试官的「信任」有什么复利效应？
q_en: What compounding effect does a solid opening have on interviewer trust?
why: 扎实的形式化会建立信任，而信任会复利：一旦面试官相信你有判断力，后面偶尔的小失误他更愿意放过、当作口误而非能力问题。开局赢下信任，等于给后半场买了容错额度。
why_en: A solid formulation builds trust that compounds — once the interviewer trusts your judgment, they forgive later minor missteps as slips rather than gaps.
options: 没有影响，面试官对每个失误都同等扣分
信任会复利：开局建立信任后，后面的小失误更易被当口误
开局越强，面试官后面越会故意刁难来找平衡
信任只在行为面试有用，技术面试不看这一项
options_en: No effect — the interviewer deducts equally for every mistake.
Trust compounds: once the opening earns it, later small slips read as misstatements.
The stronger the opening, the more the interviewer nitpicks later to rebalance.
Trust only helps in behavioral rounds; technical rounds ignore it.
optionExplanations: 并非同等扣分：面试官对已建立信任的候选人更宽容，这是人评的现实。
对；信任是复利资产，开局赢下它，后半场的小失误更容易被放过。
强开局不会招来刁难，反而降低后面被抓小辫子的概率。
技术面同样是人在评：信任照样影响他如何解读你的失误。
optionExplanations_en: Not equal deductions: interviewers are more lenient toward candidates who've earned trust — a reality of human evaluation.
Correct — trust is a compounding asset; winning it early makes later small slips easier to forgive.
A strong opening doesn't invite nitpicking; it lowers the chance of being caught out later.
Technical rounds are still judged by humans: trust still shapes how they read your mistakes.

scenario: 澄清约束时得知系统要在 50ms 内、以 100K QPS 服务在线请求（对比另一条路是可离线批处理）。
scenario_en: You learn the system must serve online at 50ms within 100K QPS (versus an alternative batch path).
q: 「50ms @ 100K QPS」这组数字对形式化的直接作用是什么？
q_en: What does '50ms at 100K QPS' directly do to the formulation?
why: 50ms @ 100K QPS 是给定的服务约束(SLO)，不是公式推出的。它直接砍掉重模型，把形式化逼向轻量模型+预计算+水平扩展。
why_en: 50ms at 100K QPS is a given serving SLO rather than a derived number, and it rules out heavy models outright, pushing the formulation toward lightweight models with precomputed features and horizontal scaling.
options: 它只影响服务器数量，不改变模型选型
给定的服务约束，直接砍掉重模型，逼向轻量+预计算
它意味着必须用最大的模型才能扛住 100K QPS
它只在离线训练时相关，在线服务不受它约束
options_en: It only affects server count, not model choice.
It's a given serving constraint that eliminates heavy models, forcing lightweight ones plus precompute.
It means you must use the largest model to withstand 100K QPS.
It only matters for offline training; online serving is unconstrained by it.
optionExplanations: 它不止是加机器：延迟+吞吐先决定哪类模型根本跑不动，再谈扩容。
对；这组数字是硬约束，直接排除大模型逐条推理，逼你走轻量+预计算的形式化。
说反了：越大的模型越进不了 50ms、越难扛 100K QPS。
在线服务恰恰被它约束：这就是在线延迟与吞吐的 SLO。
optionExplanations_en: It's more than adding machines: latency plus throughput first decide which model classes can't run at all.
Correct — these numbers are a hard constraint that rules out big per-item inference, forcing a lightweight, precomputed formulation.
Backwards: bigger models are less able to hit 50ms and harder to sustain at 100K QPS.
Online serving is precisely what it constrains — it's the online latency and throughput SLO.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求数，衡量在线吞吐；100K QPS 是高并发规模约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS (Queries Per Second) measures online throughput; 100K QPS is a high-concurrency scale constraint.

scenario: 命题「设计内容审核系统」刚说完，候选人立刻答：「用微调的 ResNet 做多标签图像分类」。
scenario_en: Right after 'design a content moderation system,' the candidate says: 'a fine-tuned ResNet for multi-label image classification.'
q: 这个开局最主要的问题是什么？
q_en: What's the primary issue with this opening?
why: 主要问题是没澄清需求就锁定方案。内容审核可能涉及文本/视频、误报误漏的政策容忍度、监管可解释性——一句 ResNet 多标签分类把这些全跳过了，是典型锚定：先有方案、再找需求合理化。
why_en: The primary issue is committing to a solution before clarifying requirements — content moderation could span text/video, FP/FN policy tolerance, and regulatory explainability, all skipped by jumping to ResNet.
options: ResNet 太旧，应该用更新的视觉 transformer
多标签分类的损失函数选错了，应该换成 focal loss
在澄清需求前就锁定了方案(锚定)，跳过模态与政策容忍度
没有先估算图像数据的存储成本
options_en: ResNet is too old; a newer vision transformer should be used.
The loss function for multi-label classification is wrong; it should be focal loss.
It commits to a solution before clarifying requirements (anchoring), skipping modality and policy tolerance.
It didn't first estimate the storage cost of the image data.
optionExplanations: 模型新旧是细枝末节：真问题是还没框问题就锁了方案。
损失函数是方案内部的事；错在根本就不该这么早进方案。
对；没澄清模态/政策/可解释性就秒定 ResNet，是教科书式锚定。
存储成本是次要约束；核心问题是过早承诺、跳过形式化。
optionExplanations_en: The model's age is a detail: the real problem is locking a solution before framing the problem.
The loss is an internal solution detail; the error is entering the solution this early at all.
Correct — committing to ResNet without clarifying modality/policy/explainability is textbook anchoring.
Storage cost is a secondary constraint; the core issue is premature commitment that skips formulation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带残差连接的经典卷积神经网络，常用于图像分类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ResNet (Residual Network) is a classic convolutional network with residual connections, common for image classification.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个样本可同时属于多个类别（如一张图既暴力又含成人内容）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-label classification lets one input belong to several classes at once (an image can be both violent and adult content).

scenario: 面对同一个模糊命题，初级和资深在「问题范围」上的处理方式不同，这条差异也写进了级别评估表。
scenario_en: On the same vague prompt, junior and senior handle 'problem scoping' differently, a row in the leveling rubric.
q: 在「问题范围划定」上，初级和资深候选人怎么做不同？
q_en: How do junior and senior candidates differ on problem scoping?
why: 初级把命题照单全收、直接开做；资深先识别子问题，再把范围收敛到影响最大的那个子问题上。识别并聚焦高影响子问题，本身就是资深信号，也让后面的深度有的放矢。
why_en: A junior takes the prompt at face value and starts building, while a senior identifies sub-problems and scopes to the highest-impact one.
tradeoff: 照单全收整个命题(范围失控) vs 识别子问题、聚焦最高影响(有的放矢)
options: 初级先识别子问题并聚焦最高影响的那个，资深直接照单全收命题
初级照单全收直接开做；资深先识别子问题再收敛范围
两者都照单全收，只是资深做得更快
初级会显式排除范围外内容，资深从不划边界
options_en: Juniors identify sub-problems and focus on the highest-impact one, seniors take the prompt at face value.
Juniors take the prompt at face value and start building; seniors identify sub-problems and scope down.
Both take it at face value; seniors just do it faster.
Juniors explicitly exclude out-of-scope items, seniors never draw boundaries.
optionExplanations: 说反了：识别并聚焦子问题是资深行为，照单全收是初级。
对；先拆子问题、聚焦最高影响的那个，范围才受控，后面的深度也有的放矢。
照单全收是初级的通病，资深不会只是「更快地」照单全收。
显式划边界（含范围外）恰恰是资深的范围决策，不是初级。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: identifying and focusing sub-problems is the senior move; taking it at face value is junior.
Correct — breaking out sub-problems and focusing the highest-impact one keeps scope controlled and later depth targeted.
Taking it at face value is the junior failing; seniors don't just do the same thing faster.
Explicitly drawing boundaries (including out-of-scope) is the senior's scope decision, not the junior's.

termDefinitions.term: problem scoping / 问题范围划定
termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个宽泛命题拆成子问题，并决定聚焦哪个、显式排除哪个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Problem scoping breaks a broad prompt into sub-problems and decides which to focus on and which to explicitly exclude.
